[[Category:Large language model]]
The '''Chinchilla prescription''', derived by [[Source:Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Conference paper)|name-author]],prescribes the compute-optimal division of a fixed training budget between model parameters and training tokens for a [[Transformer]].<ref>{{#cite:Q3164}}</ref> 

== Compute budget ==

Training compute is dominated by the matrix multiplications of the forward and backward passes and is approximated by

$$
C \approx 6\,|\theta|\,D \label{compute budget}
$$

<div class="center">
{| class="wikitable"
|-
| $C$
| Training compute in floating-point operations
|-
| $ |\theta|$
| Parameter count
|-
| $D$
| Number of training tokens
|-
| $ |\theta|D$
| Forward-pass compute cost
|-
| $ |\theta|D$
| Backward-pass compute cost
|}
</div>

== Compute-optimal allocation ==

=== Loss function ===

[[Source:Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Conference paper)|name-author]] proposes modelling [[language model loss|loss]] as a function of $\theta,D$, with an irreducible floor $L_\infty$ and parameters $|\theta|_c$, $D_c$, $\alpha_\theta$, $\alpha_D$ to be determined empirically:

$$
L(|\theta|,D)
=
L_\infty
+
\left(\frac{|\theta|_c}{|\theta|}\right)^{\alpha_\theta}
+
\left(\frac{D_c}{D}\right)^{\alpha_D},
$$

=== Algebraic optimum ===
Subject to $C = 6|\theta|D$, at optimum $L_\text{min}$

$$
\begin{cases}
|\theta|_{\text{opt}} \propto C^{\alpha_D/(\alpha_\theta+\alpha_D)} \\
D_{\text{opt}} \propto C^{\alpha_\theta/(\alpha_\theta+\alpha_D)}
\end{cases}
$$

{{Hidden proof}}
'''Solution via Lagrange multiplier'''

'''Target''':

Minimise

$$
L(|\theta|,D)=L_{\infty}+\left(\frac{|\theta|_{c}}{|\theta|}\right)^{\alpha_{\theta}}+\left(\frac{D_{c}}{D}\right)^{\alpha_D} 
$$

subject to

$$
6|\theta|D-C=0.
$$

'''Lagrangian condition''':

$$
\mathcal{L}(|\theta|,D,\lambda)
=
L_{\infty}+\left(\frac{|\theta|_{c}}{|\theta|}\right)^{\alpha_{\theta}}
+\left(\frac{D_{c}}{D}\right)^{\alpha_D}
+\lambda\,(6|\theta|D-C).
$$

'''First-order conditions at optimum'''':

$$
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial|\theta|}\bigg|_{\theta_\text{opt},D_\text{opt}}
=
-\frac{\alpha_{\theta}}{\theta_\text{opt}}\left(\frac{|\theta|_{c}}{\theta_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_{\theta}}
+\lambda\,6D_\text{opt}
=0, & \text{(2)}\\
\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial D}\bigg|_{\theta_\text{opt},D_\text{opt}}
=
-\frac{\alpha_D}{D_\text{opt}}\left(\frac{D_{c}}{D_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_D}
+\lambda\,6\theta_\text{opt}
=0, & \text{(3)}\\
\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial\lambda}\bigg|_{\theta_\text{opt},D_\text{opt}}
=
6\theta_\text{opt}D_\text{opt}-C=0. & \text{(4)}
\end{cases}
$$

<blockquote>
Equation (4) just restates the constraint. Equations (2)–(3) are the substantive conditions.
</blockquote>

'''Eliminating $\lambda$''':

From (2):

$$
\lambda=\frac{\alpha_{\theta}}{6\theta_\text{opt}D_\text{opt}}\left(\frac{|\theta|_{c}}{\theta_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_{\theta}}.
$$

From (3):

$$
\lambda=\frac{\alpha_D}{6\theta_\text{opt}D_\text{opt}}\left(\frac{D_{c}}{D_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_D}.
$$

Equate:

$$
\alpha_{\theta}\left(\frac{|\theta|_{c}}{\theta_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_{\theta}}
=
\alpha_D\left(\frac{D_{c}}{D_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_D}
\tag{5}
$$

'''Solving for the scaling exponents''':

Rearrange the terms in (5):

$$
\left(\frac{D_c}{D_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_D}
=
\frac{\alpha_\theta}{\alpha_D}
\left(\frac{|\theta|_c}{\theta_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_\theta}.
$$

Raise both sides to the $\frac{1}{\alpha_D}$th power:

$$
\frac{D_c}{D_\text{opt}}
=
\left(\frac{\alpha_\theta}{\alpha_D}\right)^{1/\alpha_D}
\left(\frac{|\theta|_c}{\theta_\text{opt}}\right)^{\alpha_\theta/\alpha_D}.
$$

Solve for $D_\text{opt}$:

$$
D_\text{opt}
=
D_c
\left(\frac{\alpha_D}{\alpha_\theta}\right)^{1/\alpha_D}
\left(\frac{\theta_\text{opt}}{|\theta|_c}\right)^{\alpha_\theta/\alpha_D}.
$$

Thus

$$
D_\text{opt}\propto\theta_\text{opt}^{\alpha_\theta/\alpha_D}.
$$

Substitute into $C=6\theta_\text{opt}D_\text{opt}$:

$$
C\propto\theta_\text{opt}^{\,1+(\alpha_\theta/\alpha_D)}
=\theta_\text{opt}^{\,(\alpha_\theta+\alpha_D)/\alpha_D}.
$$

Invert:

$$
\theta_\text{opt}\propto C^{\alpha_D/(\alpha_\theta+\alpha_D)}
$$

Similarly,

$$
D_\text{opt}\propto C^{\alpha_\theta/(\alpha_\theta+\alpha_D)}.
$$
{{End hidden}}

=== Empirical determination ===

[[File:Compute-optimal LLM Model parameter-training token balance.png|thumbnail|As seen, $D_\text{opt} \approx 20\,|\theta|_\text{opt}$ around current LLM parameter counts ($10^{10} \to 10^{12}$).|350px]]
Empirically, it was determined at the '''efficient frontier''',

$$
\frac{\alpha_\theta}{\alpha_\theta+\alpha_D}=0.46,\, \frac{\alpha_\theta}{\alpha_\theta+\alpha_D}=0.54
$$

which suggests that '''parameter count and training data size should scale nearly proportionally'''.

It is further determined experimentally

$$
D_\text{opt} \approx 20\,|\theta|_\text{opt},
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q3164}}</ref>

== History ==

[[Source:Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (Manuscript)|name-author]] had recommended spending most of an increased compute budget on parameters:

* $|\theta|_{\text{opt}} \propto C^{0.73}$
* $D_{\text{opt}} \propto C^{0.27}$

Models built to that advice were correspondingly large and undertrained.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3141}}</ref><ref>{{#cite:Q3164}}</ref>

== Experimental evidence ==

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Allocation for 3 early large language models
! Model
! $|\theta|$
! $D$
! $\frac{D}{|\theta|}$
|-
| Gopher
| $2.8\times10^{11}$
| $3\times10^{11}$
| $1.07$
|-
| GPT-3
| $1.75\times10^{11}$
| $3\times10^{11}$
| $1.71$
|-
| Chinchilla
| $7\times10^{10}$
| $1.4\times10^{12}$
| $20$
|}

Chinchilla was trained on the same compute budget as Gopher, with 4 times fewer parameters and about 5 times more data, and outperformed Gopher and GPT-3, both models several times its size.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3164}}</ref>

== Data-constrained regime and the data wall ==

If the available token stock $D_{\max}$ falls short of $D_{\text{opt}}$, the loss is better described by

$$
L_{\text{data}}(|\theta|, D_{\max})
=
L_\infty
+
\left(\frac{|\theta|_c}{|\theta|}\right)^{\alpha_\theta}
+
\left(\frac{D_c}{D_{\max}}\right)^{\alpha_D},
$$

in which case further model improvements must come from

* Increasing $|\theta|$
* Improve [[algorithmic efficiency]]
* Creation of [[synthetic data]]

This phenomenon is known as the '''[[data wall]]'''.
